thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Auto-incident INC-2024-4321 created — multiple GPU driver resets detected in inference-pool-4 (repeated Xid-style errors + container crashes). Affected nodes: node-17, node-19. Paging SRE oncall. Logs: https://logs.internal/redwood/INC-2024-4321
suneel: taking this — oncall pickup. I'll start by looking at node health and pod evictions.
suneel: quick status: node-19 shows ECC counter spike, kernel log includes repeated messages. k8s shows several runtime-proxy and model-server pods OOMKilled on node-19.
suneel: tail of dmesg on node-19: ```
[ 1234.567890] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:03:00): 31, GPU has fallen off the bus
[ 1234.567892] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:03:00): 63, Xid error, see https://nvidia.care/Xid
[ 1235.000123] kernel: Out of memory: Killed process 13456 (model-server) total-vm:...
```
eva: confirmed, node-17 is unstable too but less severe. node-19 ECC corrected-error count jumped from 2 -> 127 in 10m.
eva: suggest cordon + drain node-19 first to stop more evictions and allow reprovisioning.
suneel: cordoning/draining now: `kubectl cordon node-19 && kubectl drain node-19 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data -n inference`
ops-tilly: before draining, can we scale down large-batch consumers? We have a couple of heavy batch jobs that amplify ECC stress. If we reduce batch size for AE-model-prod it might reduce sustained GPU memory pressure.
ops-tilly: patch in place: `PATCH /model-configs/AE-model-prod {"max_batch":8}` — rolling this out now.
incident-bot: :information_source: Observability update: 2.1% of inference requests currently failing; p95 latency +120ms for inference-pool-4 since 00:34UTC. Top impacted tenant: atlas-insights (private deploy).
oncall-sre: Heads-up — customer-facing ops: open a short bridge and notify CSMs. If we need fallback, route atlas-insights critical traffic to cpu-variant endpoints.
suneel: initiated bridge: https://meet.internal/bridges/INC-2024-4321 (joining). Notifying CSM @lina.
derek: logs show driver version 541.22 loaded on nodes, there are recent vendor reports about this driver regressing on ECC handling. Rolling back to 535.86 in test pool reduced resets in staging previously.
carmen: if rollback is needed, let's avoid a full fleet rollback. Plan: reprovision new node with driver 535.86 into pool, reroute traffic, and then cordon problem nodes for maintenance.
suneel: doing a targeted reboot + driver reload on node-19: `ssh node-19 sudo systemctl restart nvidia-driver.service && sudo dmesg | tail -n 50` — will report back.
suneel: restarting now...
suneel: after restart: NVRM messages decreased but ECC counters still elevated. Model-server pods have restarted on other nodes. Starting a controlled reprovision: launching new instance template with driver 535.86 + kernel CVE backlog patch.
eva: started instance template build and test: `packer build //images/gpu-535.86.json` — will validate health checks.
ops-tilly: meanwhile, placing node-17 and node-19 in maintenance (cordoned) and evicting non-critical workloads. Leaving autoscaler to replace capacity.
suneel: cordoned node-17/node-19, evicted inference pods. Critical tenants routed to dedicated failover routes. :white_check_mark:
incident-bot: :warning: Customer impact update: atlas-insights saw 7 short-lived failures during failover window; SLO impact estimated < 0.5% for the hour. Incident severity remains SEV2 while we monitor for recurrence.
oncall-sre: CSMs notified, post-incident follow-up scheduled. We'll need to provide a timeline and RCA draft.
derek: I've queued a canary with driver 535.86 in the canary group (inference-canary). Monitoring logs for 15m before broader rollout.
carmen: handoff from suneel -> carmen at 00:58UTC. suneel, leave any open actions?
suneel: handoff notes: node-19 rebooted, driver reloaded, node cordoned, new template building, traffic rerouted to cpu-variants for atlas-insights while canary runs. Observability: error rate trending down. Handing over to carmen for driver rollback rollout and RCA.
carmen: taking over. I'll watch the canary and coordinate rollback if Xid resets reappear. I'll also start drafting customer impact blurb for CSM.
eva: monitoring dashboards — p95 latency and error-rates returning to baseline across the pool. KV cache warmup looks normal after pod restarts.
carmen: starting RCA draft: initial hypothesis — transient ECC spike + driver regression + high sustained batch pressure causing memory corruption and OOMs. Will attach logs + repro steps.
incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Update: canary on driver 535.86 (3 nodes) has been stable for 18m, no Xid resets observed. Recommend staged rollout to remaining fleet with 10% increments.
ops-tilly: scheduling rollout window for 02:00UTC with runbook steps and rollback plan.
carmen: updating incident ticket and notifying product & security as required. Next update in 30m or on significant change.
derek: one more note — collect nvml traces from node-19 to attach to RCA: `python /opt/tools/nvml_dump.py --output /tmp/nvml-node19.json`
suneel: thanks all. I'll remain reachable if any late regressions. Good handoff.
carmen: confirmed, continuing monitoring. Closing on-call handoff.
incident-bot: :information_source: INC-2024-4321 state -> MONITORING. Will auto-close if stable for 2h.
